editorial.subjectLine: June wins: branding, growth & young makers
editorial.previewText: Andrea Halal on treating your career like a GTM plan, plus tamariki wiring their first circuits in West Auckland.

founderNote.heading: A note from our founder
founderNote.bodyMd:
June was a month of range. At academyEX in Grafton, our fourth HER WAKA cohort gathered for Andrea Halal's session on personal branding — she challenged everyone to treat their career like a Go-To-Market plan, and to use LinkedIn as a tool for real relationships rather than a highlight reel.

Two Saturdays later we were in a very different room: the hall at Fruitvale Primary School, where rangatahi aged 12 to 18 built circuits, dimmed LEDs, and met Artificial Intelligence for the first time. Our Youth Tech Series with [Peyvand Academy](https://www.shesharp.org.nz/events/peyvand-academy-13-june-2026) and the Ministry of Education is about planting that first spark early — and there is nothing quite like watching a young person light up an LED they wired themselves.

From new graduates rebuilding their networks to kids discovering they can make electricity behave, the throughline is the same: everyone deserves a way in. Thank you for holding that door open with us.
founderNote.signature: Dr. Mahsa McCauley, Founder & Chair, She Sharp

photoOfTheMonth.caption: Hands on at Fruitvale Primary School: a She Sharp facilitator and a table full of young makers bring their electronics kits to life during our June Youth Tech Series.

editorial.recapIntro: Three very different rooms, one shared mission — here is what June looked like across our community.

eventBlurbs.her-waka-june-2026: At academyEX in Grafton, our fourth HER WAKA cohort worked with Andrea Halal on personal branding and career growth, with RCSA on hand to decode the current New Zealand job market.
eventBlurbs.peyvand-academy-13-june-2026: At Fruitvale Primary School, rangatahi aged 12–18 explored AI concepts and basic electronics hands-on, alongside Peyvand Academy and the Ministry of Education.
eventBlurbs.peyvand-academy-20-june-2026: Back at Fruitvale Primary School, the series went deeper into electronics — resistors, LEDs, series and parallel circuits — with Little Engineers joining Peyvand Academy and the Ministry of Education.

opportunities.title: Become a mentor
opportunities.body: A few hours a month can change the shape of someone's career. Share what you have learned with a woman finding her feet in tech.

opportunities.title: Volunteer with us
opportunities.body: From youth workshops to hackathons, our events run on volunteers. Bring your skills and grow your own network while you are at it.

opportunities.title: Support the mahi
opportunities.body: Every workshop, every LED, every new connection is powered by community generosity. Chip in to keep STEM open to everyone.

editorial.sponsorThanks: Our June events simply would not happen without our hosts and partners: academyEX for opening their Grafton space for HER WAKA, the Ministry of Social Development for backing the programme, and Peyvand Academy, the Ministry of Education, and Little Engineers for making the Youth Tech Series possible. Thank you.

heroStat.label: of NZ job ads now reference AI skills

didYouKnow.text: Auckland generates 54% of New Zealand's tech-sector GDP and employs around 68,000 tech workers — the beating heart of the country's tech economy.

recapEvents.title: Her Waka (June 2026) — Personal Branding & Growth Tips
recapEvents.shortDescription: The fourth HER WAKA cohort focuses on personal branding and career growth strategy with Andrea Halal — learn to treat your career like a Go-To-Market plan and use LinkedIn to build visibility, credibility, and genuine professional networks.
